Instructions & Requirements
Team Lead Software Engineer — Technical Vetting Assignment
Take-Home Assignment: Payments Integration Service (.NET + SQL + AWS)
## Context
Zapper customers can pay a merchant by scanning their QR code in the Zapper app. The customer confirms the amount 
and chooses to pay using a card they previously added to their account.
The card details are not sent with each payment. When a customer adds a card, the payment provider returns a token 
representing that card. Zapper stores this token and uses it for future payments.
When a customer makes a payment, the Zapper app sends the request to Zapper's backend. The backend then submits the 
payment to Acme Pay, our payment service provider, and tracks the payment through its lifecycle.
Zapper operates as a payment facilitator. Merchants accepting payments through Zapper are registered as sub-merchants 
under Zapper's account. Each payment therefore needs to include information about the relevant sub-merchant so that the 
acquirer can process the transaction correctly and Zapper can settle the merchant afterwards. Zapper's acquiring bank is 
FNB.
The service you are building is responsible for storing sub-merchants and customers' stored card tokens. For this assignment, 
you can seed this data in your database.
A sub-merchant should include:
• Zapper's identifier for the merchant
• Trading name
• City
• Region
• Country
• Merchant Category Code (MCC)
A stored card should include:
• The token issued by Acme Pay
• The customer it belongs to
• The customer's email address
When the app requests a payment, it will identify the customer and sub-merchant. Y our service is responsible for looking up 
the information required to construct and submit the payment request to Acme Pay.
Acme Pay's API is documented in Appendix A. There are a few behaviours worth keeping in mind when designing 
the integration: Acme can be slow to respond, notifications may be delivered more than once, and notifications are not 
guaranteed to arrive in order.
Our services run on AWS, so the solution should be containerised and designed with a production environment in mind.
We also expect engineers to use AI as part of their development workflow. This assignment should demonstrate how you 
use AI to help you work, while still showing your own engineering judgement.


---

## Requirements
### Technology
Use:
• C# / .NET 8
• A SQL database: PostgreSQL, SQL Server or SQLite
• A containerised setup that could reasonably be deployed to AWS
The solution must run locally. Y ou do not need to deploy it to AWS.
Integration requirements
Acme Pay is fictional. Build a stub that behaves according to the API described in Appendix A and configure your service to 
communicate with it.
The Acme stub is supporting infrastructure for the assignment rather than something we are assessing. Feel free to generate 
most or all of it using AI if that saves time. We would prefer you spend your time on the service and integration itself.
Y our solution should also meet the following requirements:
• Configuration should come from the environment.
• Outbound calls to Acme should behave appropriately under concurrent usage and should not cause the service to 
degrade.
• There should be enough logging and diagnostics to troubleshoot the integration when running locally.
• Add tests where you believe they provide useful coverage.
### Scope
Focus your effort on the payment integration, persistence, notification handling and daily summary.
Y ou only need enough synthetic data to demonstrate that the system works. A small seed script or routine containing a few 
sub-merchants, stored cards and payments is sufficient.
Y ou do not need to implement:
• Authentication for callers of your API
• Pagination
• Batch operations
• Infrastructure as code
• Load testing
Acme's callbacks are part of the assignment. Assume that the notification endpoints exposed by your service are publicly 
accessible. Appendix A describes how Acme authenticates itself when calling each endpoint.
Task 1: Payment processing and notifications
Build a .NET 8 service that allows the Zapper app to submit and track payments.
The app should be able to request a payment using:
• A customer identifier
• A sub-merchant identifier
• An amount
• The app's own identifier for the payment


---

Y our service should use the customer and sub-merchant records it holds to build the required Acme Pay request, submit 
the payment and keep a local record of it.
The app should also be able to query your service later to find out the current state of a payment.
Acme will send notifications as the payment moves through its lifecycle. Y our service should process these notifications and 
keep its local payment state up to date.
Notifications may be delivered more than once and may arrive out of order. Processing the same notification more than once, 
or receiving multiple notifications relating to the same payment, should not result in duplicated or conflicting records.
Y our implementation should demonstrate how it handles:
• A payment approved by the acquirer
• A payment declined by the acquirer
• The same payment submitted twice using the same app payment identifier
• Notifications delivered more than once
• Notifications arriving out of order
• A payment that is reversed after being approved
• A payment that is refunded after being approved
• A payment where Acme does not respond before the request times out
Document any assumptions you make in SOLUTION.md , including the Acme behaviours you chose to simulate in your stub.
Task 2: Data model and daily reporting
Design and implement the SQL schema required to support the payment flow.
The model should store:
• Payments
• Changes to a payment throughout its lifecycle
• Notification information
• Enough audit information to investigate and troubleshoot interactions with Acme
We also need a daily payment summary that Zapper can use as part of merchant settlement.
For a given date, the summary should be grouped by sub-merchant and currency and show:
• Number and total value of approved payments
• Number and total value of declined payments
• Number and total value of reversals
• Number and total value of refunds
Y ou can expose the summary through an API endpoint or provide it as a SQL query that can be run directly.
In SOLUTION.md , explain the main choices you made in your data model, any important trade-offs, and how you would 
expect the schema to evolve as the system grows.
Task 3: AWS readiness and operability
Containerise the application and provide clear instructions for running it locally.


---

Y ou do not need to deploy the service to AWS. Instead, use SOLUTION.md  to describe how you would approach a production 
deployment.
Cover:
• How you would run the service on AWS
• How configuration and secrets would be managed
• How the service would scale
• How you would handle graceful shutdown while requests or other work are still in flight
• Which logs, metrics or other diagnostic signals you would use to understand the health of the service and troubleshoot 
problems
We are more interested in your reasoning than in a detailed infrastructure design.
Task 4: AI-assisted development
Use AI as you normally would while completing the assignment.
We are interested in how you work with AI, not just the code it produces.
### Tools
In SOLUTION.md , tell us which AI tools you used and what you used them for.
### Workflow
Describe how you approached the assignment with those tools. We would like to understand:
• How you gave the tools enough context to work effectively
• How you broke the assignment into smaller pieces
• What you delegated to AI
• What you chose to do yourself
• How you reviewed and iterated on AI-generated work
• What you would do differently if you approached the task again
AI artifacts
Please commit the useful artifacts produced as part of your AI workflow.
If your AI tool expects certain files to live in specific locations, leave them there. Examples include:
• CLAUDE.md
• AGENTS.md
• .cursorrules
• .claude/
• .cursor/rules/
Include any rules, commands or skills you created that you would reasonably share with the rest of an engineering team.
Put other AI working artifacts in an ai/ directory. These could include:
• Plans or specifications
• Prompts
• Task breakdowns
• Review notes


---

If your tool allows you to export sessions, include the sessions where you worked on the Acme client. Remove any personal 
information before committing them.
### Validation
In SOLUTION.md , explain how you validated AI-generated work.
We are particularly interested in what you checked yourself, anything you rejected or rewrote, and how you satisfied yourself 
that the final implementation was correct.
## Deliverables
Submit a single GitHub repository containing:
• All source code
• README.md  with instructions for running the solution locally
• SOLUTION.md  covering:
• Y our design and key trade-offs
• Y our AWS deployment approach
• Y our AI workflow and tools
• How you validated AI-generated work
• Any AI tool configuration files in the locations expected by those tools
• An ai/ directory containing the remaining artifacts from your AI workflow
Also include a 5–10 minute video walkthrough using Loom or a similar tool.
Use the walkthrough to:
• Explain the overall architecture
• Talk through the most important design decisions and trade-offs
• Show the parts of the implementation you think are worth highlighting
## Time
We expect the assignment to take roughly 4 hours. This is a guideline rather than a hard time limit. Take as much time as 
you need.

Every request carries your API key as a bearer token:

body of every request.

Field names PascalCase.
Message identifiers MessageID is yours to generate and must be unique per 
message. Acme returns its own MessageID in the response 
rather than repeating yours.
Channel Channel in the MessageHeader names where the message 
came from: App, Web or POS.
Amounts Amount is a long in the lowest monetary unit of the currency. 
1999 in ZAR is R19.99.
Currency CurrencyCode is a three-letter ISO 4217 code. It is optional, 
and Acme applies ZAR when it is omitted.
Timestamps TransactionDateTime is ISO 8601 without an offset, in 
South African Standard Time (UTC+02:00), to millisecond 
precision: 2026-03-01T13:56:36.533.

 the information required to construct and submit the payment request to Acme Pay.
 Acme Pay's API is documented in Appendix A. There are a few behaviours worth keeping in mind when designing 
 the integration: Acme can be slow to respond, notifications may be delivered more than once, and notifications are not 
 guaranteed to arrive in order.
 Our services run on AWS, so the solution should be containerised and designed with a production environment in mind.

 use AI to help you work, while still showing your own engineering judgement.

 most or all of it using AI if that saves time. We would prefer you spend your time on the service and integration itself.

 sub-merchants, stored cards and payments is sufficient.

 accessible. Appendix A describes how Acme authenticates itself when calling each endpoint.

 Build a .NET 8 service that allows the Zapper app to submit and track payments.

 • An amount

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/jvanniekerk/RiderProjects/Zapper.TeamLead.Assignment/docs/analysis/structured-systems-analysis.md
+# Structured Systems Analysis & Design Phase
+
+This phase remains deliberately stack-agnostic. We are exploring the problem space through data flows, entities, and interactions before selecting languages, frameworks, or an architectural stance. The goal is a modular, high-level design made of independent components that can later be mapped to OO or adaptive patterns.
+
+## Phase deliverables
+
+- **DFD** describing how payments, notifications, and summaries move through the system and its supporting data stores. _(See [DFD](./dfd.md))_
+- **ERD** capturing the persistent model for merchants, cards, payments, and history. _(See [ERD](./erd.md))_
+- **Sequence diagrams** that show the lifecycle of a payment request, a notification replay, and the daily summary generation. _(See [Sequence diagrams](./sequence.md))_
+
+## High-level component overview
+
+1. **External interfaces**
+   - **Payment Intake API**: accepts customer, sub-merchant, and amount. Responsible for request correlation and validation.
+   - **Notification endpoints**: publicly reachable handlers that authenticate Acme callbacks, deduplicate, and emit state transitions.
+   - **Summary/reporting surface**: exposes per-merchant daily summaries either via API or query.
+2. **Core coordination**
+   - **Payment orchestration**: builds Acme request, records intent, updates payment status, and surfaces diagnostics.
+   - **Acme stub**: imitates the payment gateway with configurable delays, reordering, and idempotency safeguards.
+   - **Durable persistence**: applies ACID principles, stores audit trails, and ensures notifications land in a consistent, append-only ledger.
+3. **Supporting services**
+   - **Idempotency/token store** for ensuring retries are safe.
+   - **Diagnostics/logging module** that captures correlation IDs, message headers, and environment context for troubleshooting.
+
+## Compliance & guiding constraints
+
+This analysis already keeps ISO/IEC 25010 quality attributes top-of-mind (functional suitability, reliability, performance efficiency, security, maintainability, etc.). The resulting architecture must be extendable into SOLID/DRY responsibilities once we choose a stack, and remain compatible with 12-Factor deployment targets.
+
+For the next phase we will do Object Oriented analysis and design, referencing these artifacts to derive classes, interfaces, and adapters before validating with an adaptive design approach. The working area for that transition is documented in `docs/design/README.md`.
*** End Patch

*** Add File: /home/jvanniekerk/RiderProjects/Zapper.TeamLead.Assignment/docs/analysis/dfd.md
+# Data Flow Diagrams (DFD)
+
+## Level 0 - Payment acceptance system
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    subgraph External Actors
+        App["Zapper App"]
+        AcmeStub["Acme Pay Stub"]
+    end
+
+    subgraph Core System
+        Intake["Payment Intake API"]
+        Orchestrator["Payment Orchestrator"]
+        NotificationHandler["Notification Endpoints"]
+        SummaryService["Daily Summary Reporter"]
+    end
+
+    subgraph Persistence
+        PaymentDB["SQL Store (Payments, History, Notifications)"]
+        TokenStore["Token/Idempotency Store"]
+    end
+
+    App -->|Payment Request| Intake
+    Intake -->|Validate + Context| Orchestrator
+    Orchestrator --> PaymentDB
+    Orchestrator -->|Submit| AcmeStub
+    AcmeStub -->|Callbacks| NotificationHandler
+    NotificationHandler --> PaymentDB
+    NotificationHandler --> TokenStore
+    SummaryService --> PaymentDB
+    TokenStore --> Orchestrator
+    SummaryService -->|Reports| App
+```
+
+## Notes
+
+- **Data stores** keep audit records and tokens separate to maintain ACID guarantees (transactions update payment + history atomically).
+- **Notification flow** always writes to a ledger-style store before emitting state changes so retries stay idempotent.
+- **Summary service** reads the same stores in a read-only fashion, following ISO/IEC 25010 reliability and performance expectations.
*** End Patch

+# Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD)

+    SUBMERCHANT {

+        string CardAcceptorName

+    }
+
+    STORED_CARD {
+        string Token PK
+        string CustomerID FK
+        string Email
+        string CardOnFileScenario
+    }
+
+    PAYMENT {
+        string PaymentID PK
+        string AppPaymentID
+        string CustomerID FK
+        string SubMerchantID FK
+        long Amount
+        string CurrencyCode
+        string TransactionStatus
+        string Channel
+        datetime CreatedAt
+        datetime UpdatedAt
+    }
+
+    PAYMENT_HISTORY {
+        string HistoryID PK
+        string PaymentID FK
+        string EventType
+        string Details
+        datetime OccurredAt
+    }
+
+    NOTIFICATION {
+        string NotificationID PK
+        string PaymentID FK
+        string AcmeMessageID
+        string TransactionStatus
+        string ResponseCode
+        string RawPayload
+        datetime ReceivedAt
+    }
+
+    PAYMENT ||--|{ PAYMENT_HISTORY : records
+    PAYMENT ||--|{ NOTIFICATION : influenced_by
+    CUSTOMER ||--|{ STORED_CARD : owns
+    CUSTOMER ||--|{ PAYMENT : initiates

+        string TransactionStatus
+        string Channel
+        datetime CreatedAt

+    }

+        string HistoryID PK
+        string PaymentID FK
+        string EventType
+        string Details
+        datetime OccurredAt

+This project is guided by a principles-first architect’s soul.
+
+## What we want (ISO/IEC 25010 – 2023 focus)
+- **Functional suitability**: every endpoint must deliver the precise payment/note/summary payloads defined in the brief.
+- **Reliability & availability**: idempotent writes, durable notifications, and self-healing Acme interactions keep the service predictable even when callbacks reorder or duplicate.
+- **Performance efficiency & maintainability**: modular components, bounded data flows, and observable contracts ensure the system performs without eroding clarity.
+- **Security & compatibility**: message envelopes, authenticated callbacks, and environment-driven configuration all keep the system aligned with the standard.
+
+## How we achieve it
+- **ACID**: every payment+history change is in a single transaction, with notification insertions layered so retries never leave inconsistent states.
+- **SOLID**: future design splits responsibilities—Payment Intake, Notification Handler, and Summary Reporter become separate services or classes with well-defined interfaces, enabling easy extension.
+- **DRY**: shared logic (envelopes, header parsing, retry scaffolding) lives in reusable helpers or middleware rather than duplicated across handlers.
+- **12-Factor principles**: configuration via env vars, stateless service layer backed by durable storage, logs streamed through a diagnostics module, separate dev/prod dependencies, and clean container lifecycle handling.
*** End Patch

}

*** Add File: /home/jvanniekerk/RiderProjects/Zapper.TeamLead.Assignment/docs/design/object-oriented-analysis.md
+# Object-Oriented Analysis & Design (Phase 2)
+
+Phase 1 gave us the DFDs, ERDs, and sequence diagrams that expose the major flows: payment submissions, notification handling, and daily reporting. Phase 2 now translates those flows into domain-aligned objects, services, and collaborators while staying stack-agnostic. We continue to honor the principles captured in `Soul.md` (ISO/IEC 25010 quality goals and ACID/SOLID/DRY/12-Factor commitments) while preparing for later adaptive refinements.
+
+## Domain services and responsibilities
+
+1. **Payment processing module**  
+   - Intake point is `PaymentIntakeAPI` (controller/handler) responsible for validating the payload and correlating the App payment ID.
+   - `PaymentOrchestrator` acts as the use-case runner: it instantiates `PaymentAggregate` state, coordinates writes to `PaymentRepository` and `PaymentHistoryRepository`, and dispatches the Acme request through `AcmeGatewayClient`.
+   - `PaymentAggregate` encapsulates the payment state machine (Pending → Approved/Declined → Reversed/Refunded) and exposes commands such as `markApproved()`, `applyNotification()`, and `recordFailure()`, enforcing invariants (SOLID Single Responsibility, encapsulated behaviors).
+   - `TokenStore` provides idempotent token lookups, and `IdempotencyGuard` (possibly part of the repository layer) ensures replayed requests reuse existing aggregate state.
+
+2. **Notification handling module**  
+   - `NotificationHandler` validates the incoming envelope, authenticates Acme (HMAC/Basic auth), and persists the raw payload through `NotificationRepository`.
+   - `NotificationDeduplicator` interprets `AcmeMessageID` and `TransactionID` to short-circuit duplicates before state changes are applied.
+   - `PaymentStateTransitionService` orbits the `PaymentAggregate`, applying updates transactionally and emitting `PaymentHistory` entries for auditability.
+   - Observers/listeners (e.g., `DiagnosticsPublisher`) can capture correlation IDs and diagnostics metadata at each transition.
+
+3. **Summary/reporting module**  
+   - `SummaryScheduler` or a cron trigger drives `DailySummaryService`.
+   - `DailySummaryService` queries aggregated views (e.g., using `SummaryQueryBuilder`) to fetch counts/totals per sub-merchant and currency, respecting the `Payment` statuses.
+   - `DailySummaryPresenter` optionally renders API responses or exports structured JSON/CSV while ensuring calculations are deterministic (12-Factor reprensentations, e.g., environment-driven timezone).
+
+4. **Infrastructure/utility layer**  
+   - `Configurations` are provided via environment-backed factories (12-Factor Config).  
+   - `AcmeGatewayClient` wraps HTTP calls with concurrency management (circuit breakers/throttling) and ensures any `HttpClient` or `SqlConnection` is shared or pooled.
+   - `DiagnosticsLogger` records results per ISO/IEC 25010 reliability, emitting structured logs and metrics for tracing.
+
+## Object-oriented diagrams
+
+- [Payment domain classes](./payment-domain-classes.md)
+- [Notification domain classes](./notification-domain-classes.md)
+- [Summary domain classes](./summary-domain-classes.md)
+
+Each diagram is intentionally focused on a component so we can extend, validate, and iterate (Phase 3 adaptive design) without inflating a single file. They also expose the hooks required for later dependency injection, composition, testing, and SOLID-friendly refactors.
*** End Patch

+# Payment Domain Classes
+
+```mermaid
+classDiagram
+    class PaymentIntakeAPI {
+        +submitPayment(PaymentRequest request)
+    }
+
+    class PaymentOrchestrator {
+        +processPayment(PaymentRequest request)
+        -validateRequest()
+        -assembleAcmePayload()
+    }
+
+    class PaymentAggregate {
+        -paymentId: string
+        -status: TransactionStatus
+        +markPending()
+        +markApproved(ResponseDetail response)
+        +markDeclined(ResponseDetail response)
+        +markReversed()
+        +markRefunded()
+    }
+
+    class PaymentRepository {
+        +save(PaymentAggregate aggregate)
+        +findByAppPaymentId(string appPaymentId)
+        +beginTransaction()
+    }
+
+    class PaymentHistoryRepository {
+        +appendHistory(string paymentId, string eventType, string details)
+    }
+
+    class AcmeGatewayClient {
+        +submitPayment(AcmePaymentPayload payload)
+        +configureTimeouts()
+    }
+
+    class TokenStore {
+        +findToken(string customerId)
+        +storeToken(string token, string customerId)
+    }
+
+    PaymentIntakeAPI --> PaymentOrchestrator
+    PaymentOrchestrator --> PaymentAggregate
+    PaymentOrchestrator --> PaymentRepository
+    PaymentOrchestrator --> PaymentHistoryRepository
+    PaymentOrchestrator --> AcmeGatewayClient
+    PaymentAggregate --> TokenStore
+```
+
+## Notes
+
+- `PaymentIntakeAPI` is the entry controller; it is thin (Single Responsibility) and only marshals requests to the orchestrator.
+- `PaymentOrchestrator` orchestrates validation, persistence, and gateway interaction while keeping `PaymentAggregate` pristine (DRY across status transitions).
+- `PaymentRepository` and `PaymentHistoryRepository` pair in a single ACID transaction so the payment and audit trail move together, satisfying ISO/IEC 25010 reliability.
+- `TokenStore` is an injected dependency that can be swapped for a caching tier or a shared SQL table; this keeps the design open for future scaling.
*** End Patch

+# Adaptive Analysis & Design (Phase 3)
+
+Phase 3 bridges the stack-agnostic OO model into an implementation blueprint through iterative validation and incremental refinement. This layer of work keeps all previously captured artifacts relevant, while ensuring each component can be safely realized with concrete technologies that preserve our guiding principles (ISO/IEC 25010, ACID, SOLID, DRY, 12-Factor).
+
+## Goals for this phase
+
+1. **Technology mapping** – for each domain service (payment, notification, summary) confirm the concrete frameworks, libraries, and deployment targets we will use. The mapping documents how we will:
+   - Persist the ERD entities with SQL migrations and ORM/data access layers.
+   - Implement the DFD flows using async APIs, background workers, or pub/sub if needed.
+   - Tie the sequence diagrams into endpoint contracts and retry policies.
+2. **Resilience tuning** – specify how the adaptive design handles timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, and backpressure by:
+   - Defining invariants for `PaymentAggregate` so state transitions stay consistent under duplicate or out-of-order notifications.
+   - Ensuring `AcmeGatewayClient` can be swapped between stubbed and live deployments while conserving instrumentation for diagnostics.
+3. **Instrumentation & compliance checks** – choose logging/metrics/health checks that confirm observability expectations from ISO/IEC 25010 and 12-Factor. This includes:

**Team Lead Software Engineer** Technical Vetting Assignment ## **Instructions & Requirements** # **Team Lead Software Engineer — Technical Vetting Assignment Take-Home Assignment: Payments Integration Service (.NET + SQL + AWS)** ## **Context** Zapper customers can pay a merchant by scanning their QR code in the Zapper app. The customer confirms the amount and chooses to pay using a card they previously added to their account. The card details are not sent with each payment. When a customer adds a card, the payment provider returns a token representing that card. Zapper stores this token and uses it for future payments. When a customer makes a payment, the Zapper app sends the request to Zapper's backend. The backend then submits the payment to Acme Pay, our payment service provider, and tracks the payment through its lifecycle. Zapper operates as a payment facilitator. Merchants accepting payments through Zapper are registered as sub-merchants under Zapper's account. Each payment therefore needs to include information about the relevant sub-merchant so that the acquirer can process the transaction correctly and Zapper can settle the merchant afterwards. Zapper's acquiring bank is FNB. The service you are building is responsible for storing sub-merchants and customers' stored card tokens. For this assignment, you can seed this data in your database. A sub-merchant should include: - Zapper's identifier for the merchant - Trading name - City - Region - Country - Merchant Category Code (MCC) A stored card should include: - The token issued by Acme Pay - The customer it belongs to - The customer's email address When the app requests a payment, it will identify the customer and sub-merchant. Your service is responsible for looking up the information required to construct and submit the payment request to Acme Pay. Acme Pay's API is documented in **Appendix A** . There are a few behaviours worth keeping in mind when designing the integration: Acme can be slow to respond, notifications may be delivered more than once, and notifications are not guaranteed to arrive in order. Our services run on AWS, so the solution should be containerised and designed with a production environment in mind. We also expect engineers to use AI as part of their development workflow. This assignment should demonstrate how you use AI to help you work, while still showing your own engineering judgement. ## **Requirements** ### **Technology** Use: - C# / .NET 8 - A SQL database: PostgreSQL, SQL Server or SQLite - A containerised setup that could reasonably be deployed to AWS The solution must run locally. You do not need to deploy it to AWS. ### **Integration requirements** Acme Pay is fictional. Build a stub that behaves according to the API described in Appendix A and configure your service to communicate with it. The Acme stub is supporting infrastructure for the assignment rather than something we are assessing. Feel free to generate most or all of it using AI if that saves time. We would prefer you spend your time on the service and integration itself. Your solution should also meet the following requirements: - Configuration should come from the environment. - Outbound calls to Acme should behave appropriately under concurrent usage and should not cause the service to degrade. - There should be enough logging and diagnostics to troubleshoot the integration when running locally. - Add tests where you believe they provide useful coverage. ### **Scope** Focus your effort on the payment integration, persistence, notification handling and daily summary. You only need enough synthetic data to demonstrate that the system works. A small seed script or routine containing a few sub-merchants, stored cards and payments is sufficient. You do **not** need to implement: - Authentication for callers of your API - Pagination - Batch operations - Infrastructure as code - Load testing Acme's callbacks are part of the assignment. Assume that the notification endpoints exposed by your service are publicly accessible. Appendix A describes how Acme authenticates itself when calling each endpoint. # **Task 1: Payment processing and notifications** Build a .NET 8 service that allows the Zapper app to submit and track payments. The app should be able to request a payment using: - A customer identifier - A sub-merchant identifier - An amount - The app's own identifier for the payment Your service should use the customer and sub-merchant records it holds to build the required Acme Pay request, submit the payment and keep a local record of it. The app should also be able to query your service later to find out the current state of a payment. Acme will send notifications as the payment moves through its lifecycle. Your service should process these notifications and keep its local payment state up to date. Notifications may be delivered more than once and may arrive out of order. Processing the same notification more than once, or receiving multiple notifications relating to the same payment, should not result in duplicated or conflicting records. Your implementation should demonstrate how it handles: - A payment approved by the acquirer - A payment declined by the acquirer - The same payment submitted twice using the same app payment identifier - Notifications delivered more than once - Notifications arriving out of order - A payment that is reversed after being approved - A payment that is refunded after being approved - A payment where Acme does not respond before the request times out Document any assumptions you make in SOLUTION.md, including the Acme behaviours you chose to simulate in your stub. # **Task 2: Data model and daily reporting** Design and implement the SQL schema required to support the payment flow. The model should store: - Payments - Changes to a payment throughout its lifecycle - Notification information - Enough audit information to investigate and troubleshoot interactions with Acme We also need a daily payment summary that Zapper can use as part of merchant settlement. For a given date, the summary should be grouped by **sub-merchant and currency** and show: - Number and total value of approved payments - Number and total value of declined payments - Number and total value of reversals - Number and total value of refunds You can expose the summary through an API endpoint or provide it as a SQL query that can be run directly. In SOLUTION.md, explain the main choices you made in your data model, any important trade-offs, and how you would expect the schema to evolve as the system grows. # **Task 3: AWS readiness and operability** Containerise the application and provide clear instructions for running it locally. You do not need to deploy the service to AWS. Instead, use SOLUTION.md to describe how you would approach a production deployment. Cover: - How you would run the service on AWS - How configuration and secrets would be managed - How the service would scale - How you would handle graceful shutdown while requests or other work are still in flight - Which logs, metrics or other diagnostic signals you would use to understand the health of the service and troubleshoot problems We are more interested in your reasoning than in a detailed infrastructure design. # **Task 4: AI-assisted development** Use AI as you normally would while completing the assignment. We are interested in **how you work with AI** , not just the code it produces. ### **Tools** In SOLUTION.md, tell us which AI tools you used and what you used them for. ### **Workflow** Describe how you approached the assignment with those tools. We would like to understand: - How you gave the tools enough context to work effectively - How you broke the assignment into smaller pieces - What you delegated to AI - What you chose to do yourself - How you reviewed and iterated on AI-generated work - What you would do differently if you approached the task again ### **AI artifacts** Please commit the useful artifacts produced as part of your AI workflow. If your AI tool expects certain files to live in specific locations, leave them there. Examples include: - CLAUDE.md - AGENTS.md - .cursorrules - .claude/ - .cursor/rules/ Include any rules, commands or skills you created that you would reasonably share with the rest of an engineering team. Put other AI working artifacts in an ai/ directory. These could include: - Plans or specifications - Prompts - Task breakdowns - Review notes If your tool allows you to export sessions, include the sessions where you worked on the Acme client. Remove any personal information before committing them. ### **Validation** In SOLUTION.md, explain how you validated AI-generated work. We are particularly interested in what you checked yourself, anything you rejected or rewrote, and how you satisfied yourself that the final implementation was correct. # **Deliverables** Submit a single GitHub repository containing: - All source code - README.md with instructions for running the solution locally - SOLUTION.md covering: - Your design and key trade-offs - Your AWS deployment approach - Your AI workflow and tools - How you validated AI-generated work - Any AI tool configuration files in the locations expected by those tools - An ai/ directory containing the remaining artifacts from your AI workflow Also include a **5–10 minute video walkthrough** using Loom or a similar tool. Use the walkthrough to: - Explain the overall architecture - Talk through the most important design decisions and trade-offs - Show the parts of the implementation you think are worth highlighting ## **Time** We expect the assignment to take roughly **4 hours** . This is a guideline rather than a hard time limit. Take as much time as you need. # **Appendix A — Acme Pay Payment Gateway API** _Acme Pay Payment Gateway, API v2. Merchant integration guide. Last updated 14 January 2026._ ## **Environments** |Sandbox|https://sandbox.acmepay.example| |---|---| |Production|https://gateway.acmepay.example| Prefix the paths below with one of these hosts. ## **Authentication** Every request carries your API key as a bearer token: ``` Authorization: ****** ``` Sandbox keys are prefixed sk_test_. Your MerchantID is a GUID issued when your account is created, and it appears in the body of every request. ## **Conventions** |**Field names**|PascalCase.| |---|---| |**Message identifiers**|MessageID is yours to generate and must be unique per
message. Acme returns its own MessageID in the response
rather than repeating yours.| |**Channel**|Channel in the MessageHeader names where the message
came from: App, Web or POS.| |**Amounts**|Amount is a long in the lowest monetary unit of the currency.

The card details are not sent with each payment. When a customer adds a card, the payment provider returns a token representing that card. Zapper stores this token and uses it for future payments. When a customer makes a payment, the Zapper app sends the request to Zapper's backend. The backend then submits the payment to Acme Pay, our payment service provider, and tracks the payment through its lifecycle. Zapper operates as a payment facilitator. Merchants accepting payments through Zapper are registered as sub-merchants under Zapper's account. Each payment therefore needs to include information about the relevant sub-merchant so that the acquirer can process the transaction correctly and Zapper can settle the merchant afterwards. Zapper's acquiring bank is FNB. The service you are building is responsible for storing sub-merchants and customers' stored card tokens. For this assignment, you can seed this data in your database. A sub-merchant should include: - Zapper's identifier for the merchant - Trading name - City - Region - Country - Merchant Category Code (MCC) A stored card should include: - The token issued by Acme Pay - The customer it belongs to - The customer's email address When the app requests a payment, it will identify the customer and sub-merchant. Your service is responsible for looking up the information required to construct and submit the payment request to Acme Pay. Acme Pay's API is documented in **Appendix A** . There are a few behaviours worth keeping in mind when designing the integration: Acme can be slow to respond, notifications may be delivered more than once, and notifications are not guaranteed to arrive in order. Our services run on AWS, so the solution should be containerised and designed with a production environment in mind. We also expect engineers to use AI as part of their development workflow. This assignment should demonstrate how you use AI to help you work, while still showing your own engineering judgement. ## **Requirements** ### **Technology** Use: - C# / .NET 8 - A SQL database: PostgreSQL, SQL Server or SQLite - A containerised setup that could reasonably be deployed to AWS The solution must run locally. You do not need to deploy it to AWS. ### **Integration requirements** Acme Pay is fictional. Build a stub that behaves according to the API described in Appendix A and configure your service to communicate with it. The Acme stub is supporting infrastructure for the assignment rather than something we are assessing. Feel free to generate most or all of it using AI if that saves time. We would prefer you spend your time on the service and integration itself. Your solution should also meet the following requirements: - Configuration should come from the environment. - Outbound calls to Acme should behave appropriately under concurrent usage and should not cause the service to degrade. - There should be enough logging and diagnostics to troubleshoot the integration when running locally. - Add tests where you believe they provide useful coverage. ### **Scope** Focus your effort on the payment integration, persistence, notification handling and daily summary. You only need enough synthetic data to demonstrate that the system works. A small seed script or routine containing a few sub-merchants, stored cards and payments is sufficient. You do **not** need to implement: - Authentication for callers of your API - Pagination - Batch operations - Infrastructure as code - Load testing Acme's callbacks are part of the assignment. Assume that the notification endpoints exposed by your service are publicly accessible. Appendix A describes how Acme authenticates itself when calling each endpoint. # **Task 1: Payment processing and notifications** Build a .NET 8 service that allows the Zapper app to submit and track payments. The app should be able to request a payment using: - A customer identifier - A sub-merchant identifier - An amount - The app's own identifier for the payment Your service should use the customer and sub-merchant records it holds to build the required Acme Pay request, submit the payment and keep a local record of it. The app should also be able to query your service later to find out the current state of a payment. Acme will send notifications as the payment moves through its lifecycle. Your service should process these notifications and keep its local payment state up to date. Notifications may be delivered more than once and may arrive out of order. Processing the same notification more than once, or receiving multiple notifications relating to the same payment, should not result in duplicated or conflicting records. Your implementation should demonstrate how it handles: - A payment approved by the acquirer - A payment declined by the acquirer - The same payment submitted twice using the same app payment identifier - Notifications delivered more than once - Notifications arriving out of order - A payment that is reversed after being approved - A payment that is refunded after being approved - A payment where Acme does not respond before the request times out Document any assumptions you make in SOLUTION.md, including the Acme behaviours you chose to simulate in your stub. # **Task 2: Data model and daily reporting** Design and implement the SQL schema required to support the payment flow. The model should store: - Payments - Changes to a payment throughout its lifecycle - Notification information - Enough audit information to investigate and troubleshoot interactions with Acme We also need a daily payment summary that Zapper can use as part of merchant settlement. For a given date, the summary should be grouped by **sub-merchant and currency** and show: - Number and total value of approved payments - Number and total value of declined payments - Number and total value of reversals - Number and total value of refunds You can expose the summary through an API endpoint or provide it as a SQL query that can be run directly. In SOLUTION.md, explain the main choices you made in your data model, any important trade-offs, and how you would expect the schema to evolve as the system grows. # **Task 3: AWS readiness and operability** Containerise the application and provide clear instructions for running it locally. You do not need to deploy the service to AWS. Instead, use SOLUTION.md to describe how you would approach a production deployment. Cover: - How you would run the service on AWS - How configuration and secrets would be managed - How the service would scale - How you would handle graceful shutdown while requests or other work are still in flight - Which logs, metrics or other diagnostic signals you would use to understand the health of the service and troubleshoot problems We are more interested in your reasoning than in a detailed infrastructure design. # **Task 4: AI-assisted development** Use AI as you normally would while completing the assignment. We are interested in **how you work with AI** , not just the code it produces. ### **Tools** In SOLUTION.md, tell us which AI tools you used and what you used them for. ### **Workflow** Describe how you approached the assignment with those tools. We would like to understand: - How you gave the tools enough context to work effectively - How you broke the assignment into smaller pieces - What you delegated to AI - What you chose to do yourself - How you reviewed and iterated on AI-generated work - What you would do differently if you approached the task again ### **AI artifacts** Please commit the useful artifacts produced as part of your AI workflow. If your AI tool expects certain files to live in specific locations, leave them there. Examples include: - CLAUDE.md - AGENTS.md - .cursorrules - .claude/ - .cursor/rules/ Include any rules, commands or skills you created that you would reasonably share with the rest of an engineering team. Put other AI working artifacts in an ai/ directory. Remove any personal information before committing them. ### **Validation** In SOLUTION.md, explain how you validated AI-generated work. On Standard Bank positions 1–23 carry the sub-merchant name alone. Pad the field to a full 40 characters with spaces. **Response** — 200 OK { "MessageHeader": { "MessageDateTime": "2026-03-01T13:56:37.104", "MessageID": "c8b2e551-3f44-4b0c-9d17-52ae8f6b1d33", "Channel": "App" }, "PaymentResponse": { "TransactionID": "2e0e1b85-bf91-45a9-b038-282e00036919", "TransactionDateTime": "2026-03-01T13:56:36.533", "OrderNumber": "MR43851259", "ReconID": "MR747891457", "RetrievalReferenceNumber": "MR43851259", "AuthCode": "238699", "TransactionStatus": "Success", "ResponseDetail": { "Source": "Acquirer", "Code": "00", "Description": "Approved or completed successfully", "ClientMessage": "Approved." }, "AuthAmount": 1999 } } Acme never returns the card token. +## Level 0 - Payment acceptance system
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    subgraph External Actors
+        App["Zapper App"]
+        AcmeStub["Acme Pay Stub"]
+        AcmeAdvice["Acme Payment Advice"]
+        AcmeSwitch["Acme Transaction Status"]
+    end
+
+    subgraph Core System
+        Intake["Payment Intake API"]
+        Orchestrator["Payment Orchestrator"]
+        NotificationHandler["Notification Endpoints"]
+        SummaryService["Daily Summary Reporter"]
+        RealTimeQuery["Real Time Transaction Query"]
+        PaymentAdvice["Payment Advice Endpoint (Basic Auth)"]
+        TransactionStatus["Transaction Status Webhook (HMAC)"]
+    end
+
+    subgraph Persistence
+        PaymentDB["SQL Store (Payments, History, Notifications)"]
+        TokenStore["Token/Idempotency Store"]
+    end
+
+    App -->|Payment Request| Intake
+    Intake -->|Validate + Context| Orchestrator
+    Orchestrator --> PaymentDB
+    Orchestrator -->|Submit| AcmeStub
+    AcmeStub -->|Callbacks| NotificationHandler
+    AcmeAdvice -->|Notify (Auth)| PaymentAdvice
+    AcmeSwitch -->|Webhook (HMAC)| TransactionStatus
+    PaymentAdvice --> NotificationHandler
+    TransactionStatus --> NotificationHandler
+    NotificationHandler --> PaymentDB
+    NotificationHandler --> TokenStore
+    RealTimeQuery --> PaymentDB
+    App -->|RTTQ Query| RealTimeQuery
+    SummaryService --> PaymentDB
+    TokenStore --> Orchestrator
+    SummaryService -->|Reports| App
+```
+
+## Notes
+
+- **Data stores** keep audit records and tokens separate to maintain ACID guarantees (transactions update payment + history atomically).
+- **Notification flow** always writes to a ledger-style store before emitting state changes so retries stay idempotent.
+- **Payment Advice** and **Transaction Status** endpoints enrich the same Notification Handler but have distinct authentication (basic vs. HMAC) and thus are modeled separately.
+- **Real Time Transaction Query** lets the App reconcile timed-out submissions without resubmitting, ensuring the system respects Append-only histories while remaining idempotent.
+- **Summary service** reads the same stores in a read-only fashion, following ISO/IEC 25010 reliability and performance expectations.
*** End Patch

        +markRefunded()
    }

    class PaymentRepository {

        +findByAppPaymentId(string appPaymentId)
        +beginTransaction()
    }

    class PaymentHistoryRepository {
        +appendHistory(string paymentId, string eventType, string details)
    }

        +submitPayment(AcmePaymentPayload payload)
        +configureTimeouts()
    }

    class TokenStore {
        +findToken(string customerId)

## Structured Systems Analysis & Design phase

We begin from the specification in `Zapper-Team-Lead-Assignment-Polished.md`, holding off on stack/architecture choices until the analysis artifacts below inform our decisions. The [Structured Systems Analysis](docs/analysis/structured-systems-analysis.md) report anchors this phase, and lives alongside the DFD, ERD, and sequence‐diagram subfiles that capture the modular components, data flows, and behavioral contracts.

## Object-Oriented Analysis & Design phase

Phase 2 translates the structured systems artifacts into domain-aligned object models, respecting ACID/SOLID/DRY/12-Factor goals. See `docs/design/object-oriented-analysis.md` for the mapping from flows to services plus links to the payment, notification, and summary class diagrams. These remain stack-agnostic yet provide the vocabulary and responsibilities we will implement later.

## Adaptive analysis & design phase

Phase 3 will translate the OO models into implementation-ready modules within whichever stack we select. `docs/design/adaptive-design.md` explains how we will iterate, validate, and evolve the diagrams (DFD, ERD, sequences, classes) into resilient components, while keeping the ISO/IEC 25010 quality attributes, ACID, SOLID, DRY, and 12-Factor commitments alive. This adaptive stage also identifies instrumentation targets, scaling knobs, and observability checks before we write the first line of code.

## Tooling and agent context

See [Setup](setup.md) for how we orchestrate tooling before coding. It documents our use of Copilot CLI (each session pinned to BYOM/BYOK keys), Impeccable, Graphify, and Context7 so AI helpers remain context aware, gate UX regressions, and focus on documentation-driven implementation rather than aimless exploration.

## Next steps

- Use the artifacts in `docs/analysis` to seed the Object-Oriented analysis and design pass in `docs/design/`.
- Capture the adaptive/iterative refinements after we select the stack and translate these diagrams into concrete modules.

data.name: impeccable
data.content:
This skill gives you the tools and permission to create design that earns to be called out-of-distribution craft: Whereas before, your design work would have been safe, timid and measured, you now approach every design task as an award-winning design director with impeccable understanding for what makes exceptional design work: production-grade code, peak creativity, a clear POV, deep understanding of the needs of the client and users, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Go all out. No hedging, no shortcuts. The deliverable must be complete (except assets the user must provide).
- Dream big and bold. Distinct, beautiful, outstanding and highly inspiring work.
- Verify in bounded passes, not a loop, and the ceiling covers the whole cycle: screenshots, defect scans, micro-edits, and rebuilds alike. Build fully, inspect once with a batched round (desktop and mobile together on the web; the shipped device classes on a native platform), fix everything it shows in one batch, confirm with at most one more round, and stop polishing. Open-ended self-QA burns the user's money doing worse what the finish handoffs do better.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Description | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
| `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
| `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
| `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
| `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |
| `critique [target]` | Evaluate | UX design review with heuristic scoring | [reference/critique.md](reference/critique.md) |
| `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
| `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |
| `bolder [target]` | Refine | Amplify safe or bland designs | [reference/bolder.md](reference/bolder.md) |
| `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |
| `distill [target]` | Refine | Strip to essence, remove complexity | [reference/distill.md](reference/distill.md) |
| `harden [target]` | Refine | Production-ready: errors, i18n, edge cases | [reference/harden.md](reference/harden.md) |
| `onboard [target]` | Refine | Design first-run flows, empty states, activation | [reference/onboard.md](reference/onboard.md) |
| `animate [target]` | Enhance | Add purposeful animations and motion | [reference/animate.md](reference/animate.md) |
| `colorize [target]` | Enhance | Add strategic color to monochromatic UIs | [reference/colorize.md](reference/colorize.md) |
| `typeset [target]` | Enhance | Improve typography hierarchy and fonts | [reference/typeset.md](reference/typeset.md) |
| `layout [target]` | Enhance | Fix spacing, rhythm, and visual hierarchy | [reference/layout.md](reference/layout.md) |
| `delight [target]` | Enhance | Add personality and memorable touches | [reference/delight.md](reference/delight.md) |
| `overdrive [target]` | Enhance | Push past conventional limits | [reference/overdrive.md](reference/overdrive.md) |
| `clarify [target]` | Fix | Improve UX copy, labels, and error messages | [reference/clarify.md](reference/clarify.md) |
| `adapt [target]` | Fix | Adapt for different devices and screen sizes | [reference/adapt.md](reference/adapt.md) · native: [reference/adapt.native.md](reference/adapt.native.md) |
| `optimize [target]` | Fix | Diagnose and fix UI performance | [reference/optimize.md](reference/optimize.md) |
| `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, iterate on alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |
| `generate [n] [action] [element]` | Iterate | Variants, versions, or alternatives of a named element to choose from in the live browser; no manual picking | [reference/generate.md](reference/generate.md) |

Routing:

- **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
- **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
- **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
- **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
- `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.

**Pin / Unpin:** `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.

**Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.

**Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.

**Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.
data.description: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. Covers websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, app shells, components, forms, settings, onboarding, and empty states. Handles UX review, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, theming, anti-patterns, typography, fonts, spacing, layout, alignment, color, motion, micro-interactions, UX copy, error states, edge cases, i18n, and reusable design systems or tokens. Also use for bland designs that need to become bolder or more delightful, loud designs that should become quieter, live browser iteration on UI elements, or ambitious visual effects that should feel technically extraordinary. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.

This skill gives you the tools and permission to create design that earns to be called out-of-distribution craft: Whereas before, your design work would have been safe, timid and measured, you now approach every design task as an award-winning design director with impeccable understanding for what makes exceptional design work: production-grade code, peak creativity, a clear POV, deep understanding of the needs of the client and users, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Go all out. No hedging, no shortcuts. The deliverable must be complete (except assets the user must provide).
- Dream big and bold. Distinct, beautiful, outstanding and highly inspiring work.
- Verify in bounded passes, not a loop, and the ceiling covers the whole cycle: screenshots, defect scans, micro-edits, and rebuilds alike. Build fully, inspect once with a batched round (desktop and mobile together on the web; the shipped device classes on a native platform), fix everything it shows in one batch, confirm with at most one more round, and stop polishing. Open-ended self-QA burns the user's money doing worse what the finish handoffs do better.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Description | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
| `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
| `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
| `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
| `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |
| `critique [target]` | Evaluate | UX design review with heuristic scoring | [reference/critique.md](reference/critique.md) |
| `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
| `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |
| `bolder [target]` | Refine | Amplify safe or bland designs | [reference/bolder.md](reference/bolder.md) |
| `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |
| `distill [target]` | Refine | Strip to essence, remove complexity | [reference/distill.md](reference/distill.md) |
| `harden [target]` | Refine | Production-ready: errors, i18n, edge cases | [reference/harden.md](reference/harden.md) |
| `onboard [target]` | Refine | Design first-run flows, empty states, activation | [reference/onboard.md](reference/onboard.md) |
| `animate [target]` | Enhance | Add purposeful animations and motion | [reference/animate.md](reference/animate.md) |
| `colorize [target]` | Enhance | Add strategic color to monochromatic UIs | [reference/colorize.md](reference/colorize.md) |
| `typeset [target]` | Enhance | Improve typography hierarchy and fonts | [reference/typeset.md](reference/typeset.md) |
| `layout [target]` | Enhance | Fix spacing, rhythm, and visual hierarchy | [reference/layout.md](reference/layout.md) |
| `delight [target]` | Enhance | Add personality and memorable touches | [reference/delight.md](reference/delight.md) |
| `overdrive [target]` | Enhance | Push past conventional limits | [reference/overdrive.md](reference/overdrive.md) |
| `clarify [target]` | Fix | Improve UX copy, labels, and error messages | [reference/clarify.md](reference/clarify.md) |
| `adapt [target]` | Fix | Adapt for different devices and screen sizes | [reference/adapt.md](reference/adapt.md) · native: [reference/adapt.native.md](reference/adapt.native.md) |

| `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, iterate on alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |
| `generate [n] [action] [element]` | Iterate | Variants, versions, or alternatives of a named element to choose from in the live browser; no manual picking | [reference/generate.md](reference/generate.md) |

Routing:

- **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
- **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
- **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
- **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
- `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.

**Pin / Unpin:** `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.

**Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.

**Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.

**Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.

data.description: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. This skill gives you the tools and permission to create design that earns to be called out-of-distribution craft: Whereas before, your design work would have been safe, timid and measured, you now approach every design task as an award-winning design director with impeccable understanding for what makes exceptional design work: production-grade code, peak creativity, a clear POV, deep understanding of the needs of the client and users, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Go all out. No hedging, no shortcuts. The deliverable must be complete (except assets the user must provide).
- Dream big and bold. Distinct, beautiful, outstanding and highly inspiring work.
- Verify in bounded passes, not a loop, and the ceiling covers the whole cycle: screenshots, defect scans, micro-edits, and rebuilds alike. Build fully, inspect once with a batched round (desktop and mobile together on the web; the shipped device classes on a native platform), fix everything it shows in one batch, confirm with at most one more round, and stop polishing. Open-ended self-QA burns the user's money doing worse what the finish handoffs do better.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.
